source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Record the date and time of the inspection.
3. Clearly identify the building and the specific parts or areas inspected.
4. Use a checklist or standard form that covers all relevant fire safety regulations and precautions.
5. Note each regulation or precaution that was not met, providing specific details.
6. Include photographs, if possible, that highlight the issues observed.
7. Record the name and qualifications of the inspector who conducted the assessment.
8. Document the rationale for each failure – e.g., non-compliance with codes, damaged equipment.
9. Summarize the overall fire-safety status of the building, and list individual violations separately.
10. Note if corrective actions were recommended, and if the building owner/manager was informed.
11. Define a clear timeline for when the identified issues must be addressed.
12. Include contact information for the relevant authorities to whom the issue was or will be reported.
13. Keep a copy of each failed check report for
